sn1.1:1.3: “Deity” is _devatā_, which in Pali as in English is an abstract noun. Though feminine in grammatical gender, it does not imply that the deity is female.
sn1.1:1.4: “Good fellow” (_mārisa_; Sanskrit _mārṣa_, _māriṣa_) is a special term of address used by deities and sometimes by kings. The term harks back to Sanskrit _mādṛśa_, “one like me”, in the sense of having a comparable status.
sn1.1:1.9: The teaching suggests a state of poised flow, where one is neither stuck in attachments, nor restlessly straining to get somewhere else.
